messages:
pagerbot: ALERT: gpu-serving-pool-east-1 high GPU utilization + autoscaler errors detected. pool=pool-east-1, util=97.8%, queued_reqs=12134, avg_latency=2.3s, error=autoscaler:scale_up_blocked

alex: seeing the alert. confirming impact: are we throttling incoming requests or failing with 429?

mira: metrics show request throttles spiking. frontend returns 503s and some 429s from router layer when queue > 10k. autoscaler log: "scale_up request rejected: scale cap reached for team default (limit=8)"

sam: ugh—we rolled batchwindow=200ms + continuous_batching=true in the weekend rollout. That increases per-gpu memory and keeps KV cache hot but may increase the active KV footprint per request. if kv cache misses spike, throughput drops.

jess: timeline: alerts started at 3176543208, ramped over 2m. first manual scale attempts at 3176543230 failed (cap).

alex: immediate mitigation options? can we 1) bump scale cap 2) disable continuous batching 3) route heavy customers to fallback region?

mira: we can temporarily raise team cap by 4 nodes via api. doing 1) now: `POST /orgs/redwood/teams/default/scale_cap -d {"cap":12}` (exec in progress)

deploy-bot: Deploy request accepted: scale_cap bump to 12 queued. change-id=chg-78321

sam: parallel: I'll flip continuous batching off for pool-east-1 to reduce memory/kvcache pressure. Command: `infractl pool update pool-east-1 --continuous-batching=false`

ops-rita: heads-up: flipping will increase per-request latency initially but should recover throughput. I can do traffic shift after we confirm steady state.

alex: also let's reduce batchwindow to 50ms as a safety net. sam, can you apply both?

sam: applying now. logs:
```
- patching pool config: continuous_batching: true -> false
- patching batch_window: 200ms -> 50ms
- restarting pool controller to pick up config
```

sam: controller restart done. controllers report config synced at 3176543410.

jess: autoscaler events show scale requests are still queued but new nodes provisioning. ETA ~ 90s per node. queue length trending down from 12k -> 7.2k over last 60s.

mira: I see prefix-cache miss rate spiked right before incident (prefixttl flip during deploy). miss_rate went from 2% -> 28%. suspect a config flip at 3176543002. maybe a rollback didn't fully apply.

alex: who changed prefix cache TTL? need a quick audit.

mira: checking changelog... found PR #4721 merged at 3176542989 by infra-runner that set prefix_cache_ttl=0 (disable sticky keys) for experiments. that rolled to canary and then to pool-east-1. rolling back now to ttl=15m.

deploy-bot: Rollout rollback initiated: revert PR 4721 -> prefix_cache_ttl=15m. rollout-id=r-9021

sam: rollback applied to pool-east-1 at 3176543542. prefix cache miss rate slowly dropping.

jess: queue length now 2.1k, GPU util down to 78%. 503s dropping, 429s nearly gone. good signal.

csm_luis: raising to CS: several customers (IDs: cust-342, cust-129, cust-991) reported degraded responses and timeouts in last 12min. drafting message: "We experienced degraded API performance in US-East ~10:03-10:20 UTC; mitigations in progress; retries recommended. Follow-up with root cause once incident closed." any objections?

alex: send. include affected endpoints: /generate, /chat/stream. note that embeddings unaffected (different pool).

ops-rita: confirming no data loss. logs show requests were throttled not dropped. we should notify support SLAs as degraded.

sam: recommends postmortem action items: 1) gated rollout for prefix_cache_ttl experiments 2) autoscaler safety to avoid silent cap rejections (emit page early) 3) add kvcache memory pressure metric to alerts 4) revert continuous batching to default behind feature flag for pool changes.

jess: adding an immediate follow-up: add an alert that triggers when autoscaler rejects >1 scale_up in 5m with queue >5k. current alert thresholds are too permissive.

alex: summary: root cause = experimental prefix_cache_ttl change + weekend batching rollout increased per-GPU memory leading to higher kvcache misses and throughput collapse. compound failure: autoscaler cap prevented timely scaling.

alex: incident severity -> Sev2. I'll create postmortem ticket and link to this thread. Great work on the quick rollback/flip.

pagerbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied (prefix-cache rollback, continuous batching disabled, batch_window reduced, scale cap bumped). Service recovery observed at 3176543720.

csm_luis: message sent to affected customers. collecting logs/traces for follow-up.

jess: oncall handoff to night team at 3176543799. leaving notes in the incident doc.

alex: thanks everyone. if any lingering anomalies, ping this thread or @oncall-night.
